Civil Judge, Member, Additional Mact, Kundapura,
Partly Allowing The Claim Petition For Compensation
And Seeking Enhancement Of Compensation.

This Appeal, Coming On For Hearing, This Day, The
Court Delivered The Following:
 Judgment
1.
The claimant is in appeal challenging the exoneration of liability on the insurer and also seeking for enhancement of compensation.

2. The Tribunal on assessment of the evidence on record has come to the conclusion that the insurer would not be liable to pay the compensation, since there were discrepancies in the evidence adduced, which indicated that the vehicle in question was not involved in the accident and the material on record also showed that the claimant was colluding with the Police officials and the owner of the offending vehicle.

3. In order to come to this conclusion, the Tribunal has essentially relied upon the fact that in Ex.R-1, issued by Mahesh Hospital, the doctors record indicated "history of fall" whereas Ex.P-3 /
wound certificate issued by Adarsha Hospital, indicated that it was a case of an "alleged Road Traffic Accident (Pedestrian hit by a bike at Kavadi on 23.02.2014)".

The Tribunal also took note of the case- sheet by Adarsha Hospital, which was produced as Ex.P- 13, in which an earlier entry of History of bike skid and sustaining injury to the left hip was struck down and in its place, it was recorded as history of hit by a scooter and was hit by scooter while walking on the road to come to the conclusion that there is manipulation of the record and fraud was being played on the insurer.
4.

It is not in dispute that on 23.02.2014, the claimant suffered an accident and was initially taken to Mahesh Hospital at about 11.10 p.m. and the hospital records indicate that an history of fall with complaints of pain in the left leg.
This does not indicate that there was any statement made about an accident involving a motor vehicle.

However, the next hospital record of Adarsha Hospital in which the claimant was admitted on 24.02.2014 at 02.20 p.m. indicates initially that it was an history of bike skid as a result of which injury was sustained, but subsequently struck down to state that he was hit by a scooter while walking on the road.
5. The doctor from Adarsha Hospital was examined as PW-2.

He has during the course of his cross-examination stated that the claimant had informed them that he had suffered injuries when the bike in which he was travelling had a skid and as a consequence, the entry was made.

However,
there is no suggestion made to him to the effect that the entry was struck down and was over-written.

sentences.text: It has to be noticed here that the case-sheet maintained by the doctors are not amenable to the patients.
The entries made in the medical records do not contain the signature of the patients.

Thus,
when the doctor from Adarsha Hospital was not enquired or cross- examined regarding the over-writing, the said over-writing cannot be held against the claimant.
7. The first record in the hospital i.e., in Mahesh hospital merely states that it was due to a fall without reference to any motor-cycle.
This entry that is made is again not privy to the patients.
Therefore, this record is also not indicative of the fact that the claimant informed the hospital authorities that he simply had a fall.
8. The Police after investigation have lodged a charge- sheet against the rider of the bike.
No attempt is made by the insurer to examine the investigating officer and ascertain as to whether the accident actually occurred or not.
The medical evidence on record does indicate that the claimant did suffer injuries and immediately approached the hospital.

9. Merely because there are entries which do not satisfactorily indicate the manner in which the accident had taken place, it cannot be held that there was no motor vehicle accident, especially in the light of the fact that the charge-sheet had been lodged against the rider of the motor-cycle.
10. Ex.P-6/IMV report which has been produced indicates that there was damage to the wind panel of the motor- cycle.
This IMV Report therefore indicates that the motor- cycle involved did contain a damage which was in consonance with the manner in which the accident was narrated by the claimant.

11. In the light of the IMV Report and the charge-sheet, the Tribunal ought not to have come to the view that there was some manipulation in the medical records and hence, the insurer was required to be exonerated.

12. It has to be stated here that once the Tribunal has come to the conclusion that the offending vehicle was involved in the accident, as a consequence, the victim of the accident as a result of the use of the vehicle, would be entitled to proceed against the owner and the insurer.
13. The allegation of fraud will have to be specifically pleaded and proved.
On mere assertions and suspicion, fraud will not stand established.
The Tribunal has assumed that the fraud has been played, even though the ingredients were neither proved nor fraud was proved.
In this view of the matter, the finding of exoneration of the insurer is set aside and it will have to be held that the insurer is liable to pay the compensation for the accident.

14. As far as the compensation is concerned, the Tribunal has awarded the following sums:
Compensation Sl.
As awarded by No. Nature of Heads the Tribunal (In Rs.) Loss of earning capacity due to 1. 2,59,200/-

The appeal is accordingly allowed in part.
